THIS APPEAL IS COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING,

THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 30.11.2011 passed in MVC.No.5591/2009 by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - V, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru City (for short the 'Tribunal') the present appeal is preferred by respondent No.1 therein.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that, on 22.05.2009 at about 7.30 p.m., the deceased Manjunatha was traveling in a Trailer bearing registration No.KA.11.0186, which was attached to a Tractor bearing registration No.KA.11.0185 on H. Gollahalli, Channaveerana Palya road.

At that time, the driver of the Tractor drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the said vehicle near hump and due to the impact the said Manjunatha fell down and got under the wheel of the tractor because of which he got injured and died.
Petitioner No.1 is his wife and petitioner No.2 is the mother.

4. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.4,72,000/- along with 6% interest as the Tractor and Trailer was duly insured with respondent No.1 and respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners under the following heads:-
 SL.NO. HEADS OF AMOUNT IN RS.
 COMPENSATION  1. Loss of dependency 4,32,000
2 . Loss of love and affection 10,000
3. Transportation of dead body 10,000  4. Funeral and obsequies 10,000  5. Loss of estate 5,000

sentences.text: 5. Aggrieved by the same, respondent No.1 - Insurance Company has preferred this appeal on the grounds that the deceased was a gratuitous passenger and the policy is only Act Policy; the Insurance Policy does not covers the coolie; the driver was not having a valid driving license and at the time of accident the Tractor-Trailer was used for commercial purpose.
On the said grounds, it is submitted that there is a serious infraction on the part of the owner and driver of the tractor and Tribunal ought to have dismissed the claim petition.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for petitioner and respondent No.2 justifies the order of the Tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

7. The question that arises for consideration in the instant appeal is whether at the time of accident the deceased was traveling as a gratuitous passenger and was there any violation of the policy terms as alleged by respondent No.1?
8. Ex.R3 is the copy of the driving license extract and it proves that the driver of the tractor was having necessary license to drive the tractor.
On the said ground, the Tribunal in paragraph No.22 of its judgment has negated the said contention of respondent No.1.

Further, the deposition of PWs.1 &
2 goes to show that the deceased was doing coolie work.

The case of the appellant - Insurance Company is that the pleading and the documents produced as well as evidence adduced goes to show that the deceased was working as a coolie under one Shivarama and not under respondent No.2, to whom the tractor belongs.

For that they rely upon the complaint lodged by petitioner No.1 and also the deposition of PWs.1 & 2, which reveals that the deceased was working as a coolie under one Shivarama in agricultural field.
However, it also reveals that on certain occasion the deceased was being called to work as a coolie for respondent No.2 - Owner of the tractor.
The depositions and the complaint does not make it clear as to on the fateful day whether the deceased was working for respondent No.2 or not.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 in the course of arguments submits that as on the given date he had hired the services of the deceased and he had died in the course of employment.

For the said reason, the contention of the insurance company that the petitioner was an unauthorized passenger in the tractor trailer and that he was not working for respondent No.2 cannot be accepted.

Section 147 (1) The Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 as stood then, reads as under:
147. Requirement of policies and limits of liability.

- (1) In order to comply with the requirements of this Chapter, a policy of insurance must be a policy which - (a) is issued by a person who is an authorized insurer, and United India Insurance Co Limited vs Smt Sudha on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38776407/
3 (b) insures the person or classes of persons specified in the policy to the extent specified in sub-section (2)-
(i) against any liability which may be incurred by him in respect of the death of or bodily injury to any person including owner of the goods or his authorized representative carried in the motor vehicle or damage to any property of a third party caused by or arising out of the use of the motor vehicle in a public place;
(ii) against the death of or bodily injury to any passenger of a transport vehicle,
except gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle, caused by or arising out of the use of the motor vehicle in a public place.
9. Given the facts and circumstances, the deceased has to be considered as an employee of respondent No.2, who was traveling in the Tractor Trailer in the course of his employment.
10.

sentences.text: For the said reasons, I do not find any reason to interfere with the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
Hence, the appeal is hereby dismissed.
The amount-in-deposit, if any, before this Court shall be transmitted to the Tribunal for disbursement to the petitioners.
